item.text:
Swallowed gum does not stay in the stomach for seven years, so I can’t present that claim as fact. Here’s accurate copy in the requested voice.

### (a) Three posts under 280 characters

1. We’re clearing up a persistent myth: swallowed chewing gum does not stay in your stomach for seven years. Although gum isn’t fully digested, it usually passes through your digestive system.

2. We recommend putting used gum in the trash—not swallowing it. But an accidentally swallowed piece won’t remain in your stomach for seven years. That familiar warning is a myth.

3. We believe health advice should be accurate: swallowing gum does not leave it sitting in your stomach for seven years. Large amounts can rarely cause a blockage, especially in children, so we discourage swallowing it.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 105 words

We want to clear up a warning many of us heard growing up: swallowed chewing gum does not stay in your stomach for seven years. Our bodies cannot fully digest the gum base, but that does not mean it remains trapped inside us. An accidentally swallowed piece usually moves through the digestive system and leaves the body in stool. We still recommend disposing of gum rather than swallowing it, because large amounts can rarely cause a blockage, particularly in children. We believe practical health guidance starts with getting the facts right—and replacing a memorable myth with a clear explanation is a good start.
